Code of Conduct Vietnam Document Type Policy Audience All Employees Document ID POL-LE-005 POL Mandatory Confidentiality Public Language English Applies To ELCA Information Technology (Vietnam), Ltd. Release Date - Next Review - Version 1.2 Owner CHRISTOPH STETTLER Business Area Legal Author STÉPHANE ROSA st 1 Reviewer VANISHA POONAM RENGGLI Review Date - nd 2 Reviewer LAURENT WASSENBERG Review Date - Approver FREDERIC MONTIER Approval Date - Executive Summary Abstract Since its creation more than 25 years ago, ELCA’s business practices have always been driven by a high degree of honesty, transparency and compliance, as well as the adoption of many best practices in the broad industry fields where it is present. This mandatory Policy outlines the values, principles and rules that each employee must know and apply at all times. It can be shared with our suppliers and partners and ELCA has the expectation that all our 3rd party relationships behave the same. Scope This Code of Conduct is applicable to each and every employee, consultant, apprentice, trainee and otherwise staff (“the Employee(s)”) engaged by ELCA. ELCA will also take reasonable endeavors to ensure that other parties it is contracting with, such as suppliers and partners share the same values and ethics, and reasonably apply this Code of Conduct in return. Whenever relevant and feasible, ELCA will include or integrate this Code of Conduct or its principles in agreements or contracts.

Policy 1 Principles ELCA Information Technology (Vietnam), Ltd. (hereafter “ELCA”) abides by the values, principles and rules set forth in this Code of Conduct (hereafter “the Code”) and expresses its strong commitment to maintain the same high level of standard in all its activities. The Code cannot be an exhaustive list of all possible circumstances and business scenarios and may miss some situations which would deserve additional guidance. When such case occurs, Employees shall use their best judgment to stick to the spirit of the Code and, where possible, seek leadership beforehand. In any case, Employees must: • Act with honesty, integrity and legally • Protect ELCA and its reputation • Keep ELCA’s interests above and ahead of personal or other interests Vietnamese regulation and/or commonly accepted business practices should never be in contradiction with the Code. If this would occur, no activities shall take place before a review by the Legal department. ELCA Employees will receive clear communication regarding this code and its applicability and will have access to it at all times. 2 Values ELCA's values are the DNA of our company: they define who we are, the way we do business and they shape our company culture. Our values are the basis for our long-lasting success, and we articulate both why they are valuable in the market, and what concrete behaviors they drive in our interactions with partners and with each other. Collaborative: Because working together, shoulder-to-shoulder, brings first class results and mutual success. • We draw on the very best of ELCA expertise for our projects, no matter where it resides in the company • We ask for and give help wherever it is needed within ELCA, and we challenge each other to ensure the best result Well-founded: Because we are passionate about innovative thinking and technical perfection, we develop out of the box solutions, reach competitive advantages and thus add value. • We continually deepen and extend our capabilities and knowledge so that we remain truly distinctive • We build and execute internal processes that set the standard for efficiency and effectiveness • We act to ensure ELCA’s long-term performance and health, in order to sustain our mission POL-LE-005 Code of Conduct Vietnam Page 3 / 9 May not be transmitted to third parties without proper authorization template CPR 2.4 Uncontrolled copy when printed, please visit https://documentcenter.svc.elca.ch/CorporatePolicies

Independent: Because our responsibility is to deliver value, no matter what technology to use and which way to go. • We give honest, independent, fact-based advice • We take responsibility in our own ELCA roles for proactively solving problems and making decisions Committed: Because focusing on our business, working as a team and leveraging our knowledge and experience, enables us to deliver excellent solutions • We deliver the best possible solutions to generate value • We take steps to help each other, as colleagues, to learn and develop professionally Trustworthy: Because you can trust us to say what we do and do what we say • We always act with integrity • We act with candor and openness with colleagues, and our actions match our words 3 Compliance 3.1 Laws & Regulations Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations in Vietnam shall never be compromised. ELCA ensures that management staff is appropriately trained to detect when activities or projects are subject to local, national or international legislation, or industry-related regulation, and appropriately address compliance. When necessary, ELCA will create dedicated governance around a specific obligation in order to clarify it (e.g. GDPR), and Employees shall adhere to it as an obligation. Such internal governance may go beyond what is required by law. 3.2 Intellectual Property ELCA respects the property rights of others for products, publications and software, such as patents, copyrights and brand rights. If we want to use the intellectual property of others, we always obtain a license from the rights holders. We treat our own intellectual property with care and protect it from misuse by third parties. 3.3 Corporate Policies ELCA defines governance rules in the form of internal Policies, Standards and Procedures, supported by an overall business process framework called “Way of Working”. Employees shall respect, and be compliant with, all internal governance documents and rules. ELCA has implemented the concept of three lines of defense as part of its Risk Management practice to ensure that all governance controls are operating properly. 4 Risk Management An Enterprise Risk Management (“ERM”) process has been rolled-out at ELCA to identify, assess and address relevant risks in areas such as, but not limited to, Financial, Human, Legal or Operational. Roles and responsibilities are distributed within the company to ensure an adequate process at all levels and an opportunity to aggregate and escalate risks to the General Director. All senior employees are trained to report risks at their level and escalate as necessary. 5 Finance Ethics 5.1 Competition We are aware of our broad industry positioning and therefore avoid any suspicion of discriminating against competitors or business partners. Price-fixing, restrictions on services offered, bidding manipulation, discrimination and all other forms of unfair competitive behavior will not be tolerated at ELCA. We are committed to competition and the free play of market forces as the fundamental principles of the legal and economic systems found in all countries where we operate. 5.2 AML Due Diligence rd ELCA is not active in the sector of financial transactions or active financing of 3 party activities. Therefore, ELCA does not consider the presence of AML controls necessary. For the sake of clarification, ELCA Employees shall not engage in any activity or behavior related to organized crime, financing of terrorism, money laundering or illegal financial transactions. Upon notice of such behavior, Employees shall immediately report detailed information to the Audit & Risk Committee by contacting the General Director. 5.3 Anti-Bribery & Anti-Corruption ELCA complies with the anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws and best practices in Vietnam. These laws generally prohibit the direct or indirect payment (or the promise to pay) in anything of value, monetary or in kind, to any government official or private person for the purpose of obtaining or maintaining business. Although clear bribe or corruption is prohibited, licit business courtesy good practices are allowed (see also 6. Gifts, Meals & Entertainment). ELCA is committed to ensure all management staff is trained and that any reported suspicion of corruption or bribery is promptly investigated. 6 Gifts, Meals & Entertainment Outside of behaviors which are clearly falling into the bribery and corruption behaviors, ELCA recognizes that reasonable exchange of appreciation gifts to and from third parties is part of the business relationship. Employees should not be influenced, and should not try to influence, through such behaviors. Employees shall use their best appreciation of whether the overall value and frequency of meals, gifts or entertainment they offer or receive is reasonable and could not create the impression of improperly influencing the relationship in a way or the other. Where possible and acceptable, these exchanges should be mutual and balanced over time. Employees shall not solicit or accept any gift or other item of monetary value exceeding the amount of VND 5,000,000, neither for them nor for their relatives, from any person or entity seeking official action from, doing business with, or conducting activities regulated by the Company, or whose interests may be substantially affected by the performance or nonperformance of the Employees’ duties. No Employee shall be offered to or accept from any third-party gifts taking the form of money, kickbacks or similar monetary advantages independently of their value. 7 Conflicts of Interests A conflict of interests may arise when an Employee, affiliate or relative has a personal, actual or potential interest or benefit in a transaction, decision or activity performed by ELCA that can conflict with the objective interest of the latter. This includes, but is not limited to, intellectual property, supplied products or services, or financial transactions. Employees shall preventively refrain from participating in any activity, transaction or decision of the Company if they are involved in an actual or potential conflict of interests that cannot be fully avoided or fully disclosed and explained. Whenever Employees notice that they may be part of a situation of conflict of interests, a full disclosure to the management shall be made (to HR or Finance department as appropriate), so that upon acceptance the necessary safeguards and/or a proper agreement can be put in place. 8 Human Rights 8.1 Health & Safety ELCA commits to provide the safest place of work to its Employees and takes all appropriate measures to ensure a safe and healthy environment. In particular, ELCA takes appropriate measures against any significant public health situation and encourages the reporting of any hazard in facilities or activities to the management. 8.2 Discrimination & Harassment Diversity and personal dignity of Employees is of utmost importance at ELCA and engaging in harassment or discrimination based on origin, nationality, religion, race, gender, sexual orientation or age is not tolerated. Employees shall not engage in the initiation or spreading of misinformation, rumors, defamation or similar activities against each other. Employees who feel that their workplace does not comply with the above principles are encouraged to report or raise their concerns to their HR representative, their management chain, or the General Director as they feel appropriate. 8.3 Equal Opportunity Employees are one of the most important company assets at ELCA and we want to ensure that the best skills are hired independently of any criteria listed in 8.2 Discrimination & Harassment. The HR department commits to a fair selection of candidates, in avoidance of all favoritism, preference or selection related to the above and/or based on family relationship or friendship. 8.4 Data Protection Respect of privacy and protection of personal data of Employees is guaranteed. ELCA implements data protection standards based on frameworks like ISO 27701 and respects all applicable regulation including the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP) and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Employees can exercise their data privacy rights, such as access to their personal data through HR directly. 9 Reporting & Whistleblowing Employees are encouraged to report non-compliances and breaches of this Code of Conduct to the appropriate management representative depending on each case, such as the HR Department, the Chief Accountant or the General Director. Employees can address their concerns to whoever in the management chain without restriction as they feel appropriate. ELCA guarantees the protection of Employees in doing so and will prevent and/or sanction any adverse action against the Employee resulting from the reporting.
